question: Between an analysis and a final PDF, what does report generation actually consume -- and does any of it carry governed, shadow or telemetry state?
path: POST /safescope-v2/classify  ->  orchestrateShadowRequest()  ->  the PRISTINE legacy payload
POST /inspections/observations/:id/analyses  ->  InspectionService.addAnalysis()  ->  hazlenz_analyses.resultSnapshot (jsonb) + knowledgeReleaseId via resolveKnowledgeReleaseId()
reconcileDecompositionFindings() / finalizeFinding()  ->  inspection_findings (incl. knowledgeReleaseId, sourceCandidate, riskSnapshot, conclusion)
snapshotInspection()   -> frozen sourceSnapshot: spreads the finding row and copies observation.analyses VERBATIM

governedStateReachesTheFrozenSnapshot.detail: snapshotInspection() spreads the whole finding row and copies each analysis verbatim, so hazlenz_analyses.knowledgeReleaseId, inspection_findings.knowledgeReleaseId and the full resultSnapshot are all inside the frozen sourceSnapshot; generate() then adds a knowledgeProvenance block. Verified present in 41/41 frozen snapshots, so their absence from the PDF is exclusion, not absence.
governedStateReachesTheFrozenSnapshot.underShadow: every one of those values is NULL, on 45/45 analyses and 59/59 findings, with an ACTIVE release and 35 approvals present -- a decision, not an empty corpus

governedStateReachesThePDF.mechanism: canonical-report-pdf-renderer.ts projects a closed allowlist of snapshot fields. It never spreads the snapshot into a page, never serialises an object, and never enumerates keys. There is no path by which an unknown field can reach a page.

proof.result: 33/33 real frozen report snapshots render BYTE-IDENTICAL after being poisoned with 38 governed/shadow/telemetry fields stamped onto EVERY object at EVERY depth
canaries: rendering one snapshot twice, unchanged, is byte-identical once /CreationDate, /ModDate and /ID are normalised -- so an inequality would be the poison
mutating finding.conclusion and finding.hazardCategory DOES change the bytes
changing site.name DOES change the bytes (cover, executive summary and running header)
proof.naturalCanary: KG-4E's own harness wrote the literal string 'kg4e-shadow-A-<case>' into traceId and idempotencyKey. Those strings are inside 8/8 SHADOW frozen report snapshots. The word 'shadow' appears 0 times in all 8 corresponding PDFs. The exclusion was demonstrated by an accident of labelling before it was demonstrated by design.

productionCodeChangeRationale: No leakage risk was found. The renderer's allowlist already excludes every governed and shadow field by construction, so there was nothing to correct.
